# Analysis of alternatives: cooling path of a TCU zone (generated by scripts/aoa.py)

Measures from results/envelope.csv and results/time_domain.csv (simulation). Utility curves are
linear between the stated good and bad values; weights sum to 100.

| Alt | Ms max (envelope, clean+fouled) | Ms median range | Ms spread (mean max-min per zone) | corner load-on peak K | corner SP-down overshoot K | switchovers per run | cost EUR per TCU |

| A one gain set (ratio 1) | 297.86 | 1.62-3.90 | 57.90 | 2.49 | 1.80 | 128.67 | 0.00 |
| B static gain ratio | 149.11 | 1.50-5.90 | 65.93 | 1.77 | 2.58 | 80.00 | 0.00 |
| C crossover ratio (tool v0.1) | 1.70 | 1.15-1.33 | 0.48 | 4.14 | 0.55 | 26.00 | 240.00 |
| D C + Tw-Tcw scaling | 3.35 | 1.17-1.48 | 0.71 | 2.70 | 0.75 | 26.00 | 610.00 |
| E C + exchanger/valve model inversion (tool v0.2) | 1.41 | 1.21-1.40 | 0.04 | 3.26 | 0.54 | 39.33 | 970.00 |

Utility anchors: robustness Ms 1.6 -> 100, 3.0 -> 0; load-on peak 1 K -> 100, 3 K -> 0;
SP-down overshoot 0.5 K -> 100, 2.5 K -> 0; Ms spread 0.1 -> 100, 1.0 -> 0; switchovers 20 -> 100,
300 -> 0; cost 0 -> 100, 3000 EUR -> 0; PLC load by inspection of the budget (study section 7).
